answer: Stop sybils with a cedar harbor reef: an agent bonds one harbor berth. Each cycle it moors one cedar log at the reef; verifiers count its rings in the harbor register, voiding a copied or twice-claimed log, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 berths at 18x: one cedar log moors one reef berth, its rings grown in that trunk and uncuttable for a second, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents moor once, keep rights.
